title: Tractor-trailer hauling 34,000 pounds of live crabs catches fire along I-81 near Morristown - NewsBreak
text:
By Hope McAlee ,
13 hours ago
MORRISTOWN, Tenn. (WATE) — An exit ramp on I-81 North is temporarily closed after a tractor-trailer hauling around 34,000 pounds of live crabs caught fire near Morristown.
Around 8:20 a.m. Wednesday, Tennessee Department of Transportation spokesperson Mark Nagi posted about the fire. The closure in place is impacting traffic traveling north on I-81 and attempting to exit onto Highway 160/Enka Highway.
Pittman Center Volunteer Fire Department to end emergency operations A photo from the scene of the fire shows a pile of crabs that the truck was carrying spilled out of the trailer where part of the siding is missing. The photos Nagi shared do not appear to show flames, however, smoke was still present.
(Tennessee Department of Transportation) (Tennessee Department of Transportation) A preliminary report on the crash from the Tennessee Highway Patrol said the tractor-trailer was traveling along I-81 at around 7 a.m. when the driver noticed there was a rear trailer axel/brake fire. The driver then parked the tractor trailer on the shoulder of the Exit 12 ramp, which was later shut down because of the fire.
Only the trailer, which contained 34,000 pounds of crabs, caught fire, the report said.
According to THP, the trailer is being off-loaded for recovery and towing of the trailer and its contents.
11 charged in Knox County Sheriff’s Office corruption case file motion to dismiss This is a developing story. Download the WATE 6 News app or sign up for our email alerts for updates.
As of 10:50 a.m., TDOT SmartWay Map showed the closure still in place, but no major traffic slowdowns were present in the area.
